component.name: Rufus Linux
component.summary: Format and create bootable USB drives

description.p: Rufus Linux is an independent Linux port inspired by Rufus. It helps inspect, format, and write bootable images to removable media with a clear safety model: the desktop stays unprivileged; raw-disk work runs in a polkit-authorized helper.
Asks how to customize Windows 10 and 11 installations, as Rufus does: skip the TPM, Secure Boot, and RAM checks, skip the online account, create a local account, and more.
Shows progress with size, speed, and time left, in size and speed units you choose.
Offers the Super Floppy Disk partition scheme only for non-bootable formats, under its Rufus name.

Creates Windows installer USB drives from Windows ISOs, with the UEFI:NTFS boot partition and optional BIOS boot, as Rufus does. Writing and formatting now work through the system disk service, so the portable AppImage needs nothing extra installed.
Proposes the selected ISO's volume name as the USB label, as Rufus does, and shortens labels to what the chosen file system accepts.
Refreshes the desktop workbench with a neutral, flat theme in a fixed-size window laid out like Rufus, and fixes misaligned section headers, device details, and image controls.
Enables standalone VHD/VHDX conversion when qemu-nbd, nbdinfo, and nbdcopy are installed. Native packages include those providers.
Adds a verified portable AppImage desktop build and strengthens helper and polkit readiness checks.
Improves UI alignment and modal behavior, adds live USB detection, and strengthens privileged target and source validation.
